title: "Development"

This page is for people who want to change the app or build it themselves. The repository's [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/pbeens/Pete-s-PDF-to-MD/blob/main/AGENTS.md) has the full contributor guide.

## How the app is put together

| Part | What it is | Files |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop window | An **Electron** app: a web page (HTML and JavaScript) packaged as a desktop program | `electron/`, `app/` |
| Launcher | A small **Node.js** script that finds Python and starts the converter | `scripts/phase1.js` |
| Converter | A **Python** program that reads the PDF with PyMuPDF (and optionally pdf-inspector) and writes the Markdown | `scripts/extract_outline.py` |

The window and the command line run the same launcher and converter, so a conversion gives the same result either way.

## Running from source

You need **Node.js 20 or newer** (a JavaScript runtime; it includes `npm`, its package installer), **Python 3.10 or newer**, and **git**.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pbeens/Pete-s-PDF-to-MD.git
cd Pete-s-PDF-to-MD
npm install                      # Electron and the build tools
python3 -m venv .venv            # a private Python just for this project
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pymupdf pdf-inspector
npm run gui                      # open the app
```

A **virtual environment** (`.venv`) is a separate copy of Python for this project, so its libraries don't mix with anything else on your computer. The launcher uses `.venv` automatically when it exists. On Windows, use `py -m venv .venv` and `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`.

To convert from the command line:

```bash
npm run phase1 -- --input "path/to/document.pdf" --conversion-mode single
```

Options include `--out-dir`, `--conversion-mode single|major|sections`, `--include-section-metadata 0|1`, and the experimental `--text-engine hybrid`, which takes body text from pdf-inspector.

## Tests

```bash
npm test     # smoke tests, then the regression suite
```

The tests convert real PDFs and check the results, for example that footnotes aren't deleted, coded headings are found, and tables keep their words. The test PDFs live in `tests/pdfs/`, which is not committed to git; a test whose PDF is missing is skipped. The list of tests and the rules for adding one are in [`tests/TEST_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/pbeens/Pete-s-PDF-to-MD/blob/main/tests/TEST_PLAN.md).

## Builds and version letters

```bash
npm run build:mac          # release build:  dist/Pete-s-PDF-to-MD-v0.8.0e-macOS.dmg
npm run build:mac:debug    # debug build:    dist/Pete-s-PDF-to-MD-v0.8.0f-debug-macOS.dmg
```

Every build moves to the next **revision letter** (`0.8.0a`, `0.8.0b`, …), stored as `buildRevision` in `package.json`, so no two installers share a name. The letter restarts at `a` when the version changes. `npm run version:show` prints the current one.

A **debug build** shows *(debug version)* in the window title and saves each conversion in a folder named after the build, for example `Annual-Report/v0.8.0f/`. Results from earlier builds stay in their own folders, which makes before-and-after comparisons easy. `npm run gui:debug` does the same when running from source.

## Releases

```bash
npm run release:prep -- --version 0.8.0 --build
```

This checks that `package.json`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `README.md` all name the version, then makes a release build. Upload the DMG to a new release on the [Releases page](https://github.com/pbeens/Pete-s-PDF-to-MD/releases), tagged `v0.8.0`.

## This website

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from the `.qmd` files in `docs/`.

```bash
quarto preview docs     # live preview in your browser
quarto render docs      # build the site into docs/_site/
```

The Changelog page is copied from `CHANGELOG.md` when the site is rendered, so it never needs editing by hand.
